title: Belgium – Research consultancy services – ILUC modelling on Sustainable Aviation Fuels at ICAO
description: The objective is to perform modelling on ILUC values for Sustainable Aviation Fuels at the Fuels Task Group of the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO). The contractor will be requested to perform modelling of indirect land use change (ILUC) values for the production of sustainable aviation fuels (SAF), in the context of the work of the Fuels Task Group (FTG) of the Committee on Aviation Environmental Protection (CAEP) at the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) for the new CAEP cycle starting as from beginning 2025. The work of the contractor will therefore contribute to continue building the framework for SAF of the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for Civil Aviation (CORSIA). The contractor will also be requested to interact with the co-leads of the subgroup on ILUC and to provide insights and advice to the European experts at ICAO on ILUC related aspects of CORSIA.

title: LEO CONSTELLATIONS REAL-TIME RADIO RESOURCE MANAGEMENT DEMONSTRATOR - EXPRO PLUS RE-ISSUE
description: To develop an active antenna combined software and hardware demonstrator representative of a LEO satellite payload by exploiting advanced strategies for real time dynamically managing radio resources.Description: On-board satellite resource allocationstrategiesare essential for managing the distribution of limited resources from the antennas to multiple user terminals. These strategies involve dynamic allocation techniques that can adjust in real-time based on traffic demand. However, in dense traffic scenarios like onboard LEO satellites, these strategies face significant challenges. The high volume of demand can lead to congestion, resulting in increased latency and reduced QoS. Additionally, the limited on-board processing capability challenges the satellite's ability to efficiently manage traffic which leads to degraded antenna performance. Considering these challenges, the objective of this activity isto develop an active antenna combined software and hardware demonstrator representative of a LEO satellite payload by exploiting advanced strategies for dynamically managing radio resources, i.e. beamforming for real time tracking and coverage change combined with power and bandwidth allocation. Resource allocation should be defined as an optimization problem, considering factors like channelconditions, user demands, interference levels, and power constraints. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Derive real-time complex coefficients, using optimization strategies for the beamforming network. - Emulate users' movement and channel changes for proactive beam steering. - Develop models to detect and classify interference sources and use optimization techniquesfor mitigation. - Manufacture and test a proof-of-concept hardware demonstrator with a limited size active phased array and associated adaptivebeamforming, mounted on a mechanically movable platform with additional antennas located in fixed positions.

title: SATELLITE COMMUNICATION TEST-BED ON-BOARD THE INTERNATIONAL SPACE STATION (ARTES AT 3A.118) (ON DELEGATION REQUEST) RE-ISSUE
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop, deploy and operate a flexible software-defined radio communication testbedwith a frequency flexible RF front end on the International Space Station, supporting a wide range of frequencies up to Q/V band addressing 5G, signal processing and advanced techniques. Targeted Improvements: Enabling innovative and fast developments of future satcom applications from UHF to Q/V band that are difficult to achieve with on-ground testing only. Description: Nowadays, there isno capability to develop and test in-orbit novel satellite communications payload functionalities in an agile manner that suits thedemands and pace of industry. The current in-orbit test opportunities available as hosted payloads on larger missions take often yearstoget in-orbit data, whilst the faster pace in-orbit demonstration CubeSat missions lack the power and continuous connectivity capabilities needed for the testing of sophisticated telecommunications functions and for which testing on ground only is not sufficient. In this activity, a flexible software-defined radio communication testbed with a frequency flexible RF front will be designed,deployed on the International Space Station and operated, supporting a wide range of frequencies. The testbed will provide unprecedented capabilities in terms of (line-of-sight) exposure, processing power, high-bandwidth ground connectivity, enabling RD into newwaveforms, processing methods, 5G and connectivity scenarios. The testbed will be used to: - develop and test communication links at low elevation angles to increase availability and system capacity; - develop and test novel low power M2M/IoT techniques in representative interference conditions; - interactively develop and test interference mitigation, monitoring and localisation techniques, takinginto account low Earth orbit characteristics and low elevation angles; - develop and test air-interfaces related to 5G with the goal to enable the reuse of terrestrial hardware for space 5G nodes and - contribute to the evolution of the CCSDS payload data telemetry standard. The testbed will allow 24 months of operation for emulation of a wide range of payload functions in space, enabling rapid iterations in the development, deployment and testing. Footnote: On Delegation Requestactivities will only be initiated onthe explicit request of at least one National Delegation.
